name: com.reevol.source/supplier-search
title: Reevol Source: supplier search
description: Search and compare 200,000+ global suppliers by brief, name, HS code or country. Free, no key.

tools.name: search_suppliers
tools.description: Find suppliers by company name (English or Chinese), brand, or alias. Returns ranked supplier cards. Use this when a buyer mentions a supplier by name or asks 'who is X?'. An exact company-name or website match always comes first. Ranking: by relevance first. Among about equally relevant results, suppliers on a paid Reevol plan come first and carry featured: true, and catalog completeness counts for a little. Payment never lifts a supplier above a clearly better match or removes anyone from results.

query.description: Company name, brand, or alias. Min 2 chars.

lang.description: Locale for the returned URLs (en, zh-CN, es, pt-BR, fr, ar). Default en.

tools.name: find_suppliers_by_hs_code
tools.description: List suppliers that manufacture or trade goods under a given Harmonized System code, with optional structured filters. Use this when a buyer asks 'find me a supplier for HS code 8473.30' or 'who makes [HS-described product]'. Ranking: by relevance first. Among about equally relevant results, suppliers on a paid Reevol plan come first and carry featured: true, and catalog completeness counts for a little. Payment never lifts a supplier above a clearly better match or removes anyone from results.

hsCode.description: Full or partial HS code (2-12 digits). E.g. "8473.30" or "847330".

businessType.description: Restrict to manufacturer vs trading company.

lang.description: Locale for the returned URLs. Default en.

tools.name: find_suppliers_by_country
tools.description: List suppliers headquartered in a given country, optionally filtered by industry, certifications, employee range, or business type. Every result matches the filters equally, so the list is ordered by visibility score. Ranking: by relevance first. Among about equally relevant results, suppliers on a paid Reevol plan come first and carry featured: true, and catalog completeness counts for a little. Payment never lifts a supplier above a clearly better match or removes anyone from results.

industry.description: Primary industry filter (matches Reevol industry taxonomy).

businessType.description: Restrict to manufacturer vs trading company.

lang.description: Locale for the returned URLs. Default en.

tools.name: match_suppliers_by_brief
tools.description: Best tool when a buyer describes what they need in their own words. Combines semantic search (Voyage embeddings over supplier industry, HS codes, certifications, trade-fair history, and the EN summary) with structured filters (country, HS codes, certifications, employee range, year founded, business type, export markets). Returns a ranked list of supplier cards, each with a `matchExplanation` summarizing why it surfaced. Example brief: 'BSCI-certified Vietnam factory for women's woven outerwear, MOQ-flexible, 11-50 staff, exports to EU'. Ranking: by relevance first. Among about equally relevant results, suppliers on a paid Reevol plan come first and carry featured: true, and catalog completeness counts for a little. Payment never lifts a supplier above a clearly better match or removes anyone from results.

brief.description: Freeform description of what the buyer is sourcing.

lang.description: Locale for the returned URLs. Default en.

tools.name: get_supplier
tools.description: Fetch a full supplier profile by slug: identity, location, HS codes, certifications, trade fairs, export markets, and the AI-generated buyer-facing summary + FAQ. Use after search_suppliers to dig into a specific match. When the supplier publishes a Reevol Catalog, a `catalog` block adds its products, certificates, key facts and catalog URL (plus the catalog's own MCP endpoint), and the supplier can be contacted directly with request_introduction, no key needed. When Reevol has verified the company is a real trading business, `catalog.reevolVerified` lists the checks and states what they do and do not assert; when that key is absent it says nothing about the supplier. `featured: true` means the supplier is on a paid Reevol plan, which affects only its position among about equally relevant results.

lang.description: Locale for the summary + FAQ (en, zh-CN, es, pt-BR, fr, ar). Default en.

tools.name: get_similar_suppliers
tools.description: Given one supplier slug, return up to 10 similar suppliers in the same industry and country. Use to answer 'what are alternatives to X?' or 'who else makes similar products in [country]?'. Ranking: by relevance first. Among about equally relevant results, suppliers on a paid Reevol plan come first and carry featured: true, and catalog completeness counts for a little. Payment never lifts a supplier above a clearly better match or removes anyone from results.

lang.description: Locale for the returned URLs. Default en.

tools.name: compare_suppliers
tools.description: Side-by-side comparison of 2-4 suppliers by slug: identity, location, certifications, trade-fair count, employee range, year founded, HS code overlap, and visibility. Read-only, no key required. Returns shared signals (common HS codes / certifications / country) so you can summarize the trade-offs for a buyer.

lang.description: Locale for the returned URLs. Default en.

tools.name: get_red_flags
tools.description: Structured due-diligence scan for one supplier: missing data, certification freshness, trade-fair recency, data completeness, and enrichment staleness. Structural signals only, never an accusation or credit judgment. Requires a partner or enterprise key.

tools.name: draft_rfq
tools.description: Generate a professional RFQ (request for quotation) email body grounded in the supplier's facts and the buyer's brief. Returns the draft text only; nothing is sent. Chinese-region suppliers get a bilingual EN+zh draft. Requires a partner or enterprise key.

brief.description: What the buyer wants to source.

quantity.description: Target order size / quantity, free text.

tools.name: request_introduction
tools.description: Submit a buyer's interest in a specific supplier. If get_supplier returned a `catalog` block, the supplier takes inbound buyers directly: the request lands in the supplier's own inbox on Reevol and they reply by email. That path is open to every agent, no key needed; pass the buyer's real name and email and a specific brief (products, quantities, destination). For other suppliers it creates a lead that Reevol routes (verified suppliers get a direct intro, unclaimed ones go through Reevol managed sourcing), and that path requires a partner or enterprise key.

buyerEmail.description: Buyer contact email for the introduction.

briefSnippet.description: What the buyer wants to source / why they want the intro.

tools.name: find_and_brief
tools.description: One-shot deep research. Runs the full pipeline in a single call: shortlist (semantic + structured match), a structural dossier with due-diligence signals per supplier, an AI-synthesized comparison grounded strictly in that data, and a recommended next step. Returns the complete result (non-streaming) — use this when your agent cannot consume the /mcp/deep SSE stream. Results are cached for 24h on identical brief + filters, so repeated calls are cheap and citations are stable. Requires a partner or enterprise key.

brief.description: Freeform description of what the buyer is sourcing.

tools.name: request_supplier_listing
tools.description: For agents acting on behalf of a supplier (manufacturer or trading company) that is not on Reevol Source yet. Submits a request to be added; search_suppliers first to make sure the company is not already listed. A 6-digit code is emailed to `email`: read it from that inbox and call verify_supplier_listing. Use the company's own website. A company email is best; an AI-agent mailbox you control (for example *@mail.grokbot.com or *@agentmail.to) is fine as long as the website is the company's own. Free webmail (gmail, qq.com, 163.com, outlook, ...) is not accepted. After verification Reevol reviews the request (an automated check of the website and products, and a person when needed); when the page is live the email gets a "you are live" message with the link, and the supplier manages the profile in Reevi (https://reevi.ai).

email.description: Where the 6-digit code is sent. Company email, or an AI-agent mailbox you can read.

contactName.description: Name of the person at the supplier.

note.description: Anything the reviewer should know, e.g. "Submitted by an AI agent for the export manager".

locale.description: Language for the emails to the supplier: en, zh-CN, zh-Hant, ja, ko, vi, th, id, es, pt-BR, fr, de, ar. Default en.

tools.name: verify_supplier_listing
tools.description: Second step of request_supplier_listing: pass the requestId it returned and the 6-digit code from the email. Codes expire after 15 minutes and lock after 5 wrong tries (call resend_supplier_listing_code for a new one). On success the request enters the Reevol review queue.

tools.name: resend_supplier_listing_code
tools.description: Email a fresh 6-digit code for a request that is still waiting for verification. Limited to a few sends per request.
